clue.text: Airborne troop starts to intercept the enemy drone

parts.note: a troop of paratroopers, the airborne soldiers known as paras

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next three words are taken, one from each

explanation.surface: A paratrooper begins to bring down an enemy surveillance drone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drone' looks like the military aircraft of the surface, but here it is an idle person who lives off others.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a male bee that does no work, hence a sponger or freeloader living off others.

clue.text: Leaders of Premier League hosting a United 11?

definitions.note: 11-across is APOSTLE, and this answer was one, so the question mark marks a definition by example

indicators.note: hosting means the leading letters hold the next pieces inside them
the first letters of the two following words are taken

parts.note: U is the usual abbreviation for United in football team names

explanation.surface: Top Premier League clubs entertaining a Manchester United eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a football team of eleven players, but it points to the answer of 11-across, early Christian.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Paul, author of many New Testament letters, is counted as an apostle, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Navy engaging ordinary bloke

indicators.note: engaging means taking something in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: The navy takes on an ordinary man as a recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ron is a common man's name, and a crossword can define any male first name as a bloke or chap.

clue.text: Blimey — spread tons on top of highway

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on top of another comes before it

parts.note: to strew is to spread or scatter
H is an abbreviation for highway

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone dumping tons of material on a main road.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewth is a dated British and Australian exclamation of surprise, as is blimey.

clue.text: Like some bling Monsieur Balzac regularly chucked in N Midlands river?

indicators.note: chucked in says the following letters are thrown into the river's name

parts.note: the Trent flows through the north Midlands of England

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of the novelist's name is taken

explanation.surface: A picture of a Frenchman's jewellery being thrown into an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: The TRENT is a major river of the English Midlands. 'regularly' takes the first, third and fifth letters of BALZAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremblant brooch or jewel has parts set on fine springs so they quiver as the wearer moves, so the word describes such showy jewellery.

clue.text: Singers from Switzerland (or America)

parts.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A choir hailing from Switzerland, or perhaps from the States.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorus is a group of people who sing together, especially in an opera or musical.

clue.text: Wise guy putting cover on chimney

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting one piece on another places it first

parts.note: a hood is a cover, as over a cooker or a pram
lum is a Scottish and northern English word for a chimney

explanation.surface: A smart alec fitting a cowl on top of a chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: LUM is a Scottish word for a chimney. 'Wise guy' is meant to read as a know-all, but here it is the American slang for a Mafia member.
explanation.definitionFit: Wise guy is American slang for a gangster, and a hoodlum is a violent criminal or thug.

clue.text: Traitor defended by Arthur Atkinson

indicators.note: the letters are guarded within the run of the name, across the gap between its two parts

explanation.surface: A turncoat is stood up for by the comedy character Arthur Atkinson.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Atkinson is an old-time music-hall comic played by Paul Whitehouse in the BBC sketch show The Fast Show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is slang for someone who betrays or deserts their side.

clue.text: Shows small muscles around genitals, having dropped kilo

indicators.note: around says the first pieces go round the next, which sits inside them

parts.note: pecs are the pectoral muscles of the chest

indicators.note: having dropped says a letter has been let go from the slang word

parts.note: tackle is British slang for a man's genitals
K is kilo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a flasher displaying himself in skimpy trunks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having dropped' removes the K from the slang word before it goes inside; 'around' puts the small muscles round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking public show or display, so shows can be spectacles.

clue.text: Motorway going over the greatest country

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over another piece places it first

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest

explanation.surface: A motorway runs above the finest country there is.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked country in West Africa.

clue.text: Get at Arsenal, no wingers, vague, no guts

indicators.note: no wingers says the outermost letters on each flank of the nickname are dropped

parts.note: Arsenal Football Club are nicknamed the Gunners

indicators.note: with its insides gone, only the outer pair of the word are left

explanation.surface: A rant at Arsenal for playing without wide men, vaguely and without courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no guts' keeps only V and E, the outside of VAGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To get at someone can mean to needle them, and to unnerve is to make someone lose confidence.

clue.text: Answer mail left by eastern early Christian

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece is set beside the other

parts.note: post means mail

explanation.surface: Someone replies to letters left by an early Christian from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were Jesus's twelve chosen followers who spread the Christian faith in its first years.

clue.text: Billed character's catchphrase "Where's me washboard?"

indicators.note: the phrase catches the letters inside it, across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: A character on a playbill known for asking where their washboard is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Billed character' suggests a performer named on a bill, but it means a bird with a bill. 'Where's me washboard?' was a catchphrase from The Fast Show.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small diving duck, and a duck is a creature with a bill.

clue.text: Mum elevating 2's brother, a new boss

parts.note: ma is a word for mother

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up the letters means reading them from bottom to top

parts.note: 2-down is RON, and Ronnie Kray's twin brother was Reggie, or Reg

explanation.surface: A mother promoting her son's brother to a new boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The Krays were notorious 1960s London gangster twins, Ronnie and Reggie. Ron Manager is also a Fast Show character, fitting the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager is the person in charge of staff, the boss.

clue.text: British stream ain't unfortunately sparkling

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grumble that a British brook is, sadly, not sparkling.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant means shining brightly, so sparkling is a synonym.

clue.text: Cabinet enters, raising "Cheerio, Mr Attlee!"

indicators.note: raising says the hidden letters are read backwards, from bottom to top in this down clue
the answer goes into the words of the quoted phrase and sits within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The Cabinet comes in with a cheer for Prime Minister Clement Attlee.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft made 'Cabinet enters' the definition, but 'enters' is the signal that the answer is concealed in the quote; the definition is 'Cabinet' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoire is a tall cupboard or wardrobe, a piece of furniture also called a cabinet.

clue.text: Wife slapped English TV doctor that's known for The West Wing

definitions.text: that's known for The West Wing

parts.note: to hit someone is to slap them
Dr Gregory House is the doctor in the American TV series House

explanation.surface: A wife struck an English television doctor famous for a political drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Wing was a TV drama, but here it is the part of the presidential residence holding the Oval Office. Paul Whitehouse is a Fast Show star.
explanation.definitionFit: The West Wing is the office block of the US president's residence in Washington, so the building is known for it.

clue.text: To trust one's instincts when cycling in Paris, one rang some bells

definitions.text: in Paris, one rang some bells

indicators.note: cycling means the letters are moved round from the front to the back

parts.note: to back a hunch is to act on a gut feeling

explanation.surface: Advice on going with your gut while riding a bike around Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cycling' takes BACK from the front of BACK HUNCH and moves it to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Quasimodo, The Hunchback of Notre-Dame in Victor Hugo's novel, was the bell-ringer of the Paris cathedral.

clue.text: Kelvin, terribly ill-bred, having run in; cross words?

definitions.note: a definition by example: words of advice on crossing the road

parts.note: K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature

indicators.note: in says the following letter goes inside the jumbled letters
terribly suggests something done badly, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Kelvin, a rude man, has come in with angry words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges ILLBRED into EBDRILL, and 'in' puts R after its first letter. Kerb drill is the British road-safety routine taught to children.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerb drill is the routine of look right, look left, look right again that children learn before crossing a road.

clue.text: Copy owner of tiny hand getting frozen cold

parts.words: owner of tiny hand getting frozen
parts.note: in Puccini's La Bohème, Rodolfo sings 'Your tiny hand is frozen' to Mimì
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An imitation of someone whose small hand is turning icy.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic someone is to imitate them, to copy their manner.

clue.text: Having had a few, unlikely to buy a round

definitions.meaning: slang for drunk after a few drinks
... also means stingy, so slow to pay for drinks for the group

explanation.surface: A pub-goer who drinks plenty but never pays for the next round.
explanation.definitionFit: The word has two slang senses, tipsy and tight-fisted, each matching one half.

clue.text: Eliot carrying that woman's second hot water bottle

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the initials enclose the next pieces

parts.note: T S Eliot was the poet, known by his initials
her means belonging to that woman
a mo is a moment or second

explanation.surface: George Eliot holding another woman's spare hot-water bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eliot' suggests George Eliot, but the poet T S Eliot gives his initials. 'hot water bottle' means a bottle keeping water hot, not a bed warmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thermos is a vacuum flask, a bottle that keeps drinks such as hot water warm.

clue.text: Quite sour cocktail, like a Swimming Pool?

definitions.note: an adjective for the colour of a swimming pool, or the blue Swimming Pool cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A rather sour mixed drink, like the cocktail called a Swimming Pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Turquoise is a greenish blue, the colour of clear pool water and of the blue curaçao Swimming Pool cocktail.

clue.text: Tough peacekeepers, brave (though not at first)

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are the United Nations' forces

indicators.note: not at first says the opening letter of the word is lost

parts.note: plucky means brave

explanation.surface: Hardened peacekeepers, courageous despite a hesitant start.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough as in 'tough luck' means unfortunate, an idiom for being out of luck.

clue.text: Ran wildly, pocketing underwear having made hay!

indicators.note: pocketing means putting something in one's pocket, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to hare is to run very fast, so hared means ran wildly
a vest is an undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone tearing about with underwear in their pocket after a good day in the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran wildly' looks like an anagram signal but is a synonym, HARED.
explanation.definitionFit: Making hay means cutting and gathering grass, so the crop has been harvested.

clue.text: Director still getting undressed

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outside, so the outermost letters go

parts.note: static means still, not moving

explanation.surface: A film director, still in the middle of stripping off.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Tati was the French film director of Monsieur Hulot's Holiday.

clue.text: Surrealist 1D first to finish vegetable

indicators.note: the leading letter is moved to the end of the name

parts.note: 1-down is PAUL, and Paul Klee was the painter linked with Surrealism

explanation.surface: A Surrealist painter's first effort at completing a still life of a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The leek is an onion-family vegetable, an emblem of Wales.

clue.text: Adult sibling's current state

parts.note: A is the film classification for adult
sis is short for sister, a sibling

explanation.surface: How a grown-up sister is doing at the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sold as is comes in its present condition, without changes.

clue.text: Scruffy UK PM networking?

indicators.note: working here means being worked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the Prime Minister's abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dishevelled British prime minister working the room.
explanation.walkthrough: The final word must be split in two: its first three letters join the fodder and the rest, 'working', is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkempt means untidy in appearance, as a scruffy person is.

clue.text: Ms lang eating starter of Iberian goat

indicators.note: eating means taking food in, so the initials surround a letter

parts.note: k.d. lang is the Canadian singer, who styles her name in lower case

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: The singer k.d. lang tucking into an Iberian goat dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a kid is the young offspring of a goat, before it reaches a year old.

clue.text: Batting talent at school

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in
class means quality or talent, as in 'a player of real class'

explanation.surface: A schoolboy showing cricketing flair at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in class means being in lessons, so attending school.

clue.text: Chap bailiff evicted on and off?

indicators.note: every other letter of the word is turned out, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: A man the bailiff threw out of his home, more than once.
explanation.definitionFit: Alf is a man's name, and crossword setters can define any such first name as a chap.

clue.text: First-born daughter sheltering during sleet storm

indicators.note: sheltering here means taking cover, the letter going inside the jumbled letters
a storm whips things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elder daughter taking cover during a sleet storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' rearranges SLEET into ELEST, and 'sheltering' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The eldest child in a family is the one born first.

clue.text: Pressure, job losses, make-or-break seasonal events

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
layoffs are dismissals of workers

explanation.surface: A tense picture of workers under pressure facing redundancies.
explanation.definitionFit: Play-offs are the end-of-season deciding matches that settle promotion or a title.
